slot.brief: Show several orderings of elements by electron gain enthalpy (including Cl vs F and positive values for noble gases); identify the incorrect one.

stem: Using signed (algebraic) electron gain enthalpy values, which ordering is incorrect?

verdicts.working: Signed electron gain enthalpies are approximately Cl −349, F −328, Br −325, I −295 kJ mol⁻¹, so the ascending order is Cl < F < Br < I. Thus (A) is correct and (D) is incorrect. (B) and (C) also follow the ascending signed values.

working:
$\text{Cl}(-349) < \text{F}(-328) < \text{Br}(-324) < \text{I}(-295)$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
$\text{S}(-200) < \text{Se}(-195) < \text{Te}(-190) < \text{O}(-141)$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
For noble gases, $\text{Xe}(+77) < \text{Ar}(+96) < \text{Ne}(+116)$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.
Thus, only D gives an incorrect order.

Independent check: Signed electron gain enthalpies are approximately Cl −349, F −328, Br −325, I −295 kJ mol⁻¹, so the ascending order is Cl < F < Br < I. Thus (A) is correct and (D) is incorrect. (B) and (C) also follow the ascending signed values.
solution: For signed electron gain enthalpies, more negative values are smaller. Since $\text{Cl}(-349)<\text{F}(-328)<\text{Br}(-325)<\text{I}(-295)$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, the ascending order is $\text{Cl}<\text{F}<\text{Br}<\text{I}$. Hence (A), which places F before Cl, is the incorrect ordering.
